input.label: Input
input.purpose: The raw image enters the network as a 3-D tensor of pixel intensities: height × width × channels (1 channel for grayscale).
input.details: Nothing is learned here. Pixel values are scaled to [0, 1] so that the first layer's weighted sums start in a well-behaved range.

conv2d.label: Conv2D
conv2d.purpose: Feature extraction. Each filter is a small learned kernel that slides over every spatial position and responds strongly wherever its pattern (an edge, a corner, a curve) appears.
conv2d.details: Weights are shared across positions (translation equivariance) and each output only sees a local k×k window of every input channel (local connectivity). Stacking conv layers grows the receptive field so deeper filters respond to larger, more abstract patterns.
conv2d.math: Y_{i,j,k} = \phi\Big(b_k + \sum_{u=0}^{K_h-1}\sum_{v=0}^{K_w-1}\sum_{c=0}^{C_{\text{in}}-1} W_{u,v,c,k}\; X_{s i+u,\; s j+v,\; c}\Big)

maxPooling2d.label: MaxPooling2D
maxPooling2d.purpose: Spatial downsampling. Keeps only the strongest response in each P×P window, halving the resolution while preserving which features were detected.
maxPooling2d.details: No parameters. Provides a small amount of translation invariance and cuts computation for later layers. During back-propagation the gradient flows only to the arg-max position of each window.
maxPooling2d.math: Y_{i,j,c} = \max_{0 \le u, v < P} X_{s i + u,\; s j + v,\; c}

averagePooling2d.label: AveragePooling2D
averagePooling2d.purpose: Spatial downsampling by averaging each P×P window, as in the original LeNet-5 “subsampling” layers.
averagePooling2d.details: No parameters. Smoother than max pooling: every input in the window receives an equal share of the gradient.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.purpose: Regularisation. During training a random fraction p of activations is zeroed so the network cannot rely on any single feature; at inference it is the identity.
dropout.details: TensorFlow.js uses inverted dropout: surviving activations are scaled by 1/(1 − p) during training, so nothing needs rescaling at inference time. The feature maps you see here are inference-mode, identical to the input.
dropout.math: \tilde X = \frac{M \odot X}{1 - p},\quad M_{ijc} \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1 - p)\ \ (\text{training});\qquad \tilde X = X\ \ (\text{inference})

flatten.label: Flatten
flatten.purpose: Reshape. Unrolls the H × W × C feature volume into one long vector so fully-connected layers can consume it.
flatten.details: No parameters and no arithmetic — just a change of indexing (row-major, channels last). Spatial layout is discarded from here on.
flatten.math: y_{(i W + j) C + c} = X_{i,j,c}

dense.label: Dense
dense.purpose: Fully-connected combination. Every output unit is a weighted sum of all inputs, letting the network combine detected features into class evidence.
dense.details: Holds most of the parameters in small CNNs. The final Dense layer outputs one unnormalised score (logit) per class.
dense.math: \mathbf y = \phi\big(W^{\top}\mathbf x + \mathbf b\big),\quad W \in \mathbb R^{n_{\text{in}} \times n_{\text{out}}}

softmax.label: Softmax
softmax.purpose: Converts logits into a probability distribution over the classes: positive values that sum to one.
softmax.details: Trained jointly with the categorical cross-entropy loss, whose gradient with respect to the logits is simply p − y.

models.name: TinyShapeNet
models.description: A compact modern CNN: two conv/max-pool stages, dropout and a small classifier head. Trains to high accuracy on the shapes dataset in a few seconds.

models.name: LeNet-5 (1998 style)
models.description: LeCun et al.'s classic: tanh convolutions with average-pooling “subsampling”, then three fully-connected layers. Padded first convolution handles 28×28 inputs, as the original padded MNIST to 32×32.

models.name: Plain MLP (no convolutions)
models.description: A fully-connected baseline that flattens the image immediately. Compare its parameter count and learned weights with the CNNs.
